claims.text: Adding a small amount of B2O3 to ceramic powders lowers the required sintering temperature.
B2O3 lowers the sintering temperature by promoting liquid-phase formation.
The B2O3-induced liquid phase enhances mass transport at reduced temperatures.
A B2O3 addition of 1–5 wt% is suitable as a sintering aid for the proposed ceramic powders.
B2O3 can be introduced during initial powder processing by dry or wet mixing.
B2O3-containing ceramics can be pressurelessly sintered at temperatures 100–200 °C below the undoped baseline.
B2O3 forms a transient liquid phase at lower temperatures in the ceramic powder compact.
The transient liquid phase increases particle diffusion and the densification rate.
The B2O3-containing phase reduces the onset temperature for sintering.
The liquid B2O3-containing phase provides a pathway for mass transport that enhances densification at lower temperatures.
B2O3-doped samples will attain equivalent or higher densification at temperatures up to 200 °C below those used for undoped samples.
Undoped ceramic powder requires a higher sintering temperature to achieve density comparable to that of B2O3-doped powder.
B2O3 contents above 5 wt% may produce excessive liquid phase.
Excessive liquid-phase formation at B2O3 contents above 5 wt% may degrade mechanical properties.
The achievable temperature reduction and mechanical performance depend on the ceramic system, processing route, and B2O3 content.
